title: Econ Priority Index (EPI): cost-latency-resilience roadmap scoring model
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Create a pragmatic prioritization framework (Econ Priority Index, EPI) that blends traditional RICE with explicit cost and latency economics, plus a resilience penalty for degraded fallback modes. Purpose: give product and GTM clear, repeatable scores to rank roadmap bets against OKRs (latency SLOs, cost-per-inference reduction, availability).
background_and_problem_statement: We use RICE-like scoring and several ad-hoc cost/latency spreadsheets today (see PM-5172 and associated decks), but decisions are inconsistent across PMs and engineering. Recent Dedicated onboarding requests surfaced trade-offs where high-reach features caused disproportionate token-cost increases or violated latency targets. We need a single numeric index that: (1) integrates reach/impact/confidence/effort, (2) explicitly accounts for delta unit cost and latency sensitivity, and (3) penalizes options that increase reliance on lower-availability fallbacks. This will drive consistent roadmap tradeoffs and feed into OKR-level prioritization.
proposed_model_overview: EPI is a multiplicative index composed of four pillars: ReachWeight, NetImpact, EconMultiplier and ResiliencePenalty. ReachWeight captures user/usage scope; NetImpact is the product of perceived product impact and Confidence; EconMultiplier captures cost-per-token delta normalized by expected token volume and latency-sensitivity; ResiliencePenalty increases score when a feature relies on degraded fallback models or cross-region failovers. The final index is scaled so it can be compared directly to current RICE outputs and mapped to priority buckets (Invest, Monitor, Defer).
scoring_formula: EPI = ReachWeight * NetImpact * EconMultiplier * (1 - ResiliencePenalty). Where: ReachWeight = normalized active-users * usage-frequency factor; NetImpact = ImpactScore * Confidence; EconMultiplier = 1 / (1 + CostDeltaNormalized * LatencySensitivityFactor); ResiliencePenalty = fallbackReliance * fallbackRiskScore. Higher EPI -> higher priority.
thresholds_and_buckets: EPI >= 0.65: Invest (high priority, candidate for Q1 OKR commit)
EPI < 0.30: Defer (low priority or research spike only)
Bucket mapping will be adjustable per-OKR stretch targets and will be tuned with first 6 weeks of telemetry after rollout.
data_sources_and_metrics: Console telemetry: per-route p50/p95 latency, error rates
Token cost model: $/1k tokens per model variant from billing data
Usage profile: expected token length distribution from product analytics
Availability metrics: fallback invocation frequency from runtime logs
A/B experiment results and evals comparing perceived quality/impact
implementation_plan: Week 0-1: Finalize formula and default normalization constants (PM + Research + Applied ML)
Week 1-2: Instrument queries for required telemetry in Console dashboards (ENG-2432)
Week 2-3: Build an EPI calculator spreadsheet and a lightweight web tool in the Console to compute scores for candidate features
Week 3-4: Pilot EPI on 6 roadmap candidates across Runtime, Console, and Dedicated; collect feedback
Week 4-6: Tune thresholds, document playbook (how to interpret scores), and integrate into quarterly roadmap reviews
Post-rollout: Automated EPI recomputation nightly and alerting for score drift relative to OKR targets
acceptance_criteria: EPI calculator exists (spreadsheet + Console prototype) and can produce scores from live telemetry
At least 6 roadmap candidates scored and used in an internal prioritization review
Stakeholder alignment from Eng, Design, Sales, and CS (recorded approvals in doc)
Thresholds and buckets documented with examples and decision rules
Easy tie-back from EPI to OKRs and to release commitments (i.e., can mark Invest items in roadmap)
